answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when independent audits confirm fabricated work or collusion. A Sybil attacker must lock capital for every identity, then risks losing it when a randomly selected raven auditor checks claims against signed task receipts; shared control or repeated evidence can trigger a coordinated review. The stake raises the cost of flooding the economy, while honest agents recover theirs. A plume of cheap accounts may gather at one knoll, but each still needs capital at risk.
